# Vendored font sources

## `font8x8_*.h` - 8x8 monochrome bitmap fonts

Author: Daniel Hepper `<daniel@hepper.net>`
Upstream: https://github.com/dhepper/font8x8
License: **Public Domain**

Quote from the header of each file:

> 8x8 monochrome bitmap fonts for rendering
> Author: Daniel Hepper <daniel@hepper.net>
> License: Public Domain
>
> Based on:
>     Marcel Sondaar
>     International Business Machines (public domain VGA fonts)
> License:
>     Public Domain

These files are vendored verbatim from
`https://github.com/dhepper/font8x8` (commit HEAD as of the import
date) so a source diff stays tractable. The conversion to Rust const
data lives under `src/fonts/*.rs` and is generated by
`psoxide-dev gen-fonts` (a Rust parser, one-shot, output
committed).

### Bit layout (font8x8)

Each glyph is 8 bytes, one byte per row. Within a byte, **bit 0 is
the leftmost pixel** (LSB-first). The `BitmapFont::bit_order` field
carries `BitOrder::Lsb` for these and preserves the convention
downstream into the upload + draw paths.

## `IBM_VGA_8x16.bin` - 8×16 IBM VGA BIOS font

Upstream: https://github.com/spacerace/romfont (path
`font-bin/IBM_VGA_8x16.bin`, extracted from an IBM VGA BIOS
ROM dump).
License of bitmap data: **Public Domain**.

This is the canonical 1981 IBM VGA character-generator ROM content
- the same data that ships in every VGA-era PC BIOS and can be
found in hundreds of projects (Linux `font_8x16.c`, FreeDOS
kernel, dhepper's font8x8 series, int10h.org's "oldschool PC
fonts," etc.). The bitmap bytes themselves have no enforceable
copyright claim (IBM published the exact glyph bitmaps in the
PC/AT technical reference manuals and made no proprietary claim at
the time of VGA's 1987 release).

Format: 256 glyphs × 16 bytes each, one byte per row, **MSB-first**
within each byte (bit 7 = leftmost pixel, matching IBM convention).
Total 4096 bytes.

### Bit layout (IBM VGA 8×16)

8-pixel-wide glyphs → one byte per row. `BitmapFont::bit_order` is
set to `BitOrder::Msb` for this font; the uploader's row-unpacker
(see [`BitmapFont::glyph_row_packed`]) normalizes both LSB and MSB
sources to the same internal representation.

## Why these instead of e.g. Linux `font_*.c`

Linux's kernel fbcon fonts are GPL-2.0 licensed even though the
bitmap data itself is universally considered PD. Shipping under a
plain PD grant via projects dedicated to PD redistribution is
simpler to reason about for bundled SDK font data. The visual output
is the same IBM-VGA look - these are all derivatives of the same
1981 IBM character-generator ROM.

## `spleen-LICENSE` - Spleen 5x8

Author: Frederic Cambus
Upstream: https://github.com/fcambus/spleen (`spleen-5x8.bdf`)
License: **BSD-2-Clause** (full text in `spleen-LICENSE`)

Spleen is a monospaced bitmap font family; the 5x8 size is the
smallest readable ASCII cell and suits dense guest UI (tables,
spreadsheets) where the 8x8 fonts waste horizontal space. Only the
converted Rust const data is vendored (`src/fonts/spleen_5x8.rs`,
U+0020..U+007E, MSB-first rows, generated from the upstream BDF);
the BDF itself is not checked in. BSD-2-Clause requires reproducing
the copyright notice and disclaimer in binary distributions, which
`spleen-LICENSE` satisfies; downstream discs that embed this font
should carry the same notice (see `docs/downstream-licensing.md`).

## `kenney-fonts/*.ttf` - Kenney Fonts

Author: Kenney
Upstream: https://www.kenney.nl/assets/kenney-fonts
License: **CC0-1.0**

The archive is vendored under `kenney-fonts/` with its upstream
`License.txt`. These fonts are intentionally useful for game UI:
blocky, square, pixel, compact and sci-fi display styles. The Rust
font modules are generated by rasterizing the TTFs into fixed-cell
1bpp ASCII-window atlases via `psoxide-dev gen-fonts`.

## `google-fonts/*/*.ttf` - Google Fonts open-source families

Upstream: https://github.com/google/fonts
Licenses: **SIL Open Font License 1.1** and **Apache-2.0**

Each vendored family directory keeps its upstream license file
(`OFL.txt` for OFL families, `LICENSE.txt` for Apache families). The
families currently imported for editor UI font choices are:

- `pressstart2p`
- `silkscreen`
- `pixelifysans`
- `orbitron`
- `audiowide`
- `michroma`
- `electrolize`
- `oxanium`
- `rajdhani`
- `chakrapetch`
- `tektur`
- `tomorrow`
- `zendots`
- `turretroad`
- `tiny5`
- `jersey10`
- `spacemono`
- `brunoace`
- `aldrich`
- `syncopate` (Apache-2.0)
- `sharetechmono`
- `jura`

These are rasterized to generated Rust bitmap modules rather than
loaded dynamically. The editor can expose the full list, while cooked
runtime manifests reference only the font modules used by authored UI
text.

## `itchio/drippy-space/DrippySpace-Regular.ttf` - Drippy Space

Author: Syntaxes of Play (`eerieA`)
Upstream: https://synofplay.itch.io/drippy-space-futuristic-sci-fi-display-font
License: **SIL Open Font License 1.1** (`itchio/drippy-space/OFL.txt`)

Drippy Space is a minimalist futuristic display face intended for titles,
logos, HUD accents, and short interface labels. The author notes that it has
only basic glyph coverage, so it is kept as a display option rather than a
general prose font. The Rust bitmap module is generated from the vendored TTF
with `psoxide-dev gen-fonts`.
